correctness.rationale: All partial permutations are vertices because they are distinct 0–1 cube points. Direct deletion counts yield exact single and disjoint inclusion probabilities; the Kronecker covariance has an exhaustive four-way orthogonal tensor decomposition. Strict gaps: (q-p)b>0, pb>0; for the remaining gap, p!t^p L_p^(q-p)(-1/t) has distinct negative zeros by the simple-positive Laguerre zero theorem (q-p>-1), giving Poisson-binomial matching size and positive variance of distinct transformed roots. This proves the first gap exactly. At fixed p, the size p-1 matching weight is p/q+O_p(q^-2) relative to size p and all smaller weights are O_p(q^-2), giving the covariance condition number q+O_p(1). The included self-contained exact arithmetic checker corroborates entries and eigenspaces for finite profiles but is not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is exclusively the 2<=p<q rectangular uniform-vertex case with a four-class strict inertia hierarchy, its exact Laguerre-root variance gap, and fixed-p linear condition-number law. The available square-case result has only three eigenspaces; two-row interior-volume moments are a different measure. The inspected 2018, 2020 and 2023 primary polytope papers enumerate vertices or study other invariants rather than establish these exact comparisons. Related scholarly searches returned John and combinatorial matching-polytope work but no stronger rectangular vertex-uniform covariance result. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The complete strictly ordered four-mode covariance spectrum classifies every extremal axis of a natural infinite family of genuinely rectangular matching polytopes. The row and column contrast modes are provably nondegenerate only when the part sizes differ. A Laguerre-root variance identity explains the smallest spectral separation, and the linear fixed-short-side condition-number law quantifies anisotropy qualitatively different from the known square case. The claim is an exact invariant classification with structural content, not an arbitrary numerical instance or a re-count of known vertices.
